title: Transport of immersed constructibility stratifications and finite module models across a clopen partition
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions whose images cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A constructible stratification here means a finite disjoint covering by immersed locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] whose images are constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset]; empty strata are permitted.

For every such stratification $(s_
u:S_
u\hookrightarrow X)_{
u\in J}$ and every $i$, the immersed schemes $S_
u	imes_X X_i\hookrightarrow X_i$, with their fibre-product scheme structures, form a constructible stratification of $X_i$. Conversely, for any constructible stratifications $(s_{i,
u}:S_{i,
u}\hookrightarrow X_i)_{
u\in J_i}$, the composites $j_i s_{i,
u}$ form a constructible stratification of $X$, indexed by the finite set $ igsqcup_iJ_i$. The stratum schemes and their structures are unchanged in this second construction.

Let $A$ be any finite commutative ring and let $F$ be a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use ordinary module inverse images with their canonical constant-ring identifications [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. If $F|_{S_
u}$ is locally constant with finite $A$-module models [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf], then the restricted stratification on $X_i$ trivializes $F|_{X_i}$ with those same models on the base-changed trivializing covers. If stratifications of the $X_i$ trivialize $F|_{X_i}$ with chosen locally constant finite-module models, the union stratification trivializes $F$ with exactly those models and covers. Thus $F$ is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] if and only if each $F|_{X_i}$ is constructible. The assertions include empty components and the empty cover of the empty scheme; if the definition requires a positive number of strata, one empty stratum may be used.

proof.text: Add the given constructibility fields to the finite locally closed stratification to obtain Scheme.Stratification X. Apply [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] along j_i. Its domains and immersions are the actual fibre products and second projections. Its range equations, local closedness, constructibility, disjointness and covering fields give exactly clopenStratification_pullback. This works with zero or empty strata.

source.place: Tag 005J and the cited immersed-stratification pullback

proof.text: For each sigma index (i,n), compose the existing stratum immersion with j_i. Composition preserves immersions and its image is j_i of the original stratum image. This image is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-image-retrocompact-open]: the range of j_i is closed, so intersecting it with a compact open is compact, hence the range is retrocompact. Within a component use injectivity of j_i and the old disjointness; across components use the given disjointness of ranges. The component and stratum covering equalities give the sigma-indexed covering equality. This proves clopenStratification_union without changing any domain scheme.

The fixed-module inverse-image compositor identifies the encoded composite intrinsic tensor pullback with the encoded iterated intrinsic tensor pullback. Lift the isomorphism through the fully faithful equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-encoding]. These comparisons use the published canonical coefficient maps, not an arbitrary coefficient action. For the fibre-product square combine the two compositors with its equation.

It yields exactly the required base-changed objects, their covering property, and the same modules. Restrict the isomorphism of step 3 over each member and compose with its model. This proves clopenStratification_pullback_models.

proof.text: For each component stratum restrict the composite comparison from step 3 over each of the supplied cover members, then compose with the supplied model isomorphism. No stratum scheme, cover object, covering arrow or module is altered. This proves clopenStratification_union_models.

proof.text: Convert intrinsic constructibility to fixed-module finite-model constructibility using [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility]. For the forward direction pull back its stratification. On each stratum, [lem-pur-proetale-finite-local-constancy-pullback], transported through the encoding and its finite-local-constancy comparison, preserves finite local models; the pullback-square equation and fixed-module compositors identify the desired restriction. For the reverse direction choose a stratification on each component, use step 2 for the sigma-indexed union, and reindex the finite sigma type by Fin of its cardinality. The fixed-module compositor transports its finite local models to the composite immersions. Convert back using the constructibility encoding comparison. Its existing positive-stratification argument covers a zero-cardinality union on the empty scheme. Thus no nonempty partition, stratum, component, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is added.
